newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: F&N soft drink unit sees profit doubling.
newsitem.headline: F&N soft drink unit sees profit doubling.

text.p: Fraser & Neave's soft drink unit F&N Coca-Cola, sees its pretax profit doubling in the fiscal year ending September 30, 1997, its president and chief operating officer Burke McKinney said on Monday.

"We are going to meet all the targets set out in December. Volume growth will be at over 20 percent, cash operating profit growth in excess of 50 percent and we will double profit in 1997," said McKinney, referring to pre-tax profit, not attributable.
He was speaking at a briefing for analysts and reporters on the F&N group's performance for six-months ended March 31, 1997.
For the year ended September 30, 1996, the soft drinks unit made a pre-tax profit of Singapore $27.97 million.
McKinney had made similar projections in December after F&N's 1996 results.
However, for the first half of its fiscal year, its profit before interest and tax slipped to S$16.56 million compared to S$22.26 million for the same period last year.
F&N said soft drink earnings were hit by the loss of three months production due to a labour strike in Sri Lanka, severe price discounting in Pakistan and heavy investment in distribution in Vietnam.
McKinney remained optimistic the soft drink unit would achieve its targets dispite the first-half performance.
"We are confident in achieving our targets. We will see very strong growth in the next six months," he said.
Growth was seen from every country it has operations in, including Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam, Sri Lanka, Nepal and Pakistan: "Everyone of them," McKinney said. "I'm not being flippant about it."
He said operations in Sri Lanka had resumed in mid-March, prices in Pakistan had stablised and Vietnam was beginning to contribute.
The company, which had made an acquisition in Hyderabad, Pakistan, also sees exceptional growth in Indochina, with over 100 percent growth in Hanoi.
McKinney said the division's investment in Vietnam, hurt by the weak dong, was "real close to breakeven if we don't make money in Vietnam".
